<div class="nv-rule" id="declaration">

## A case with no written value counts on from the one before it, starting at zero

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#declaration"><code>enums/declaration</code></a>
</div>

An enum body is a comma list of `Name` or `Name = <integer literal>`, and the optional `: int` or
`: uint` before it names the backing type ([`enums/one-backing-type`](/docs/rules/enums/#one-backing-type "Every enum is backed by exactly one integer type, and nothing else backs one")):

```
enum Status { Active, Banned }
enum Permission: uint { Read = 0b001, Write = 0b010, Admin = 0b100 }
```

The first case with no written value is `0`; every later case with no written value is the previous
case's value plus one, whether that previous value was written or counted. An explicit value resets
the counter for everything after it. A value may be negative or zero, and auto-increment continues
from a negative one.

Two cases may carry the same value. Nothing forbids the alias, because equality over an enum is
value equality and there is no identity for two names to collide on.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>Every case has an integer value even where none is written, so PHP's valueless pure case does not exist</p>
</aside>

<div class="nv-rule" id="no-case-keyword">

## PHP's `case` keyword does not parse, and each one is diagnosed where it is written

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#no-case-keyword"><code>enums/no-case-keyword</code></a>
</div>

There is no `case` keyword in an enum body. `case Hearts = 1;` is refused with **`E0239`**, raised
on the `case` keyword itself and naming the comma-list spelling that works
([`enums/declaration`](/docs/rules/enums/#declaration "A case with no written value counts on from the one before it, starting at zero")).

The case is *kept*: only the keyword and its `;` are consumed, so an enum written PHP's way still
declares every member the rest of the program goes on to name, and one diagnostic per case is the
whole answer rather than a cascade of unresolved names behind it.

This is deliberately not `E0220` ([`enums/no-class-machinery`](/docs/rules/enums/#no-class-machinery "A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases")). A method or a constant in an
enum body belongs somewhere else and is told so; a case belongs exactly where it is written, and
only its spelling is wrong.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>case Hearts = 1;</code> is not a spelling this language has — an enum body is a comma list</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/enums/#declaration" title="A case with no written value counts on from the one before it, starting at zero"><code>enums/declaration</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#no-class-machinery" title="A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases"><code>enums/no-class-machinery</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0010.md">record 0010</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-syntax/src/parser/tests/decl.rs"><code>crates/nvs-syntax/src/parser/tests/decl.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="closed-integer-type">

## An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#closed-integer-type"><code>enums/closed-integer-type</code></a>
</div>

`enum Status { Active, Banned }` declares a new named integer type with a fixed set of cases, and
the enum's name is then a type like any other — a property, a parameter, a return, a local, a class
constant, an `array<T>` element, an `Iterator<T>` yield, a `foreach` binding. The `enum` keyword
appears only at the declaration site; every use site spells the enum's own name, exactly as a class
does.

A case is a compile-time constant of that type, never an object. There is no singleton to allocate,
no identity distinct from the value ([`enums/no-class-machinery`](/docs/rules/enums/#no-class-machinery "A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases")), and no per-isolate storage
slot to build or tear down ([`enums/representation`](/docs/rules/enums/#representation "An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is")).

The set is closed, and closed means checked: a value no case names never becomes a case by default
or by silent coercion. `EnumName` is its own kind of type atom rather than a class reference, so a
name that resolves to an enum is not a class name and is never treated as one.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>An enum is not a class in disguise — a case is a compile-time constant, with no singleton, no allocation and no identity</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/enums/#declaration" title="A case with no written value counts on from the one before it, starting at zero"><code>enums/declaration</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#one-backing-type" title="Every enum is backed by exactly one integer type, and nothing else backs one"><code>enums/one-backing-type</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#no-class-machinery" title="A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases"><code>enums/no-class-machinery</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#representation" title="An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is"><code>enums/representation</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0010.md">record 0010</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007.md">record 0007</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0008.md">record 0008</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-case-is-its-integer.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-case-is-its-integer.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-crosses-a-method-boundary.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-crosses-a-method-boundary.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-typed-property-round-trips.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-typed-property-round-trips.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-is-returned-and-stored-in-an-array.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-is-returned-and-stored-in-an-array.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

<div class="nv-rule" id="one-backing-type">

## Every enum is backed by exactly one integer type, and nothing else backs one

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#one-backing-type"><code>enums/one-backing-type</code></a>
</div>

`enum E: int` and `enum E: uint` name the backing type; with no `: T` written it is `int`. Nothing
else backs an enum — `enum E: string` is refused with **`E0219`**, and so is a case whose value is
not an integer literal.

PHP's three shapes collapse into this one. There is no *pure* enum: the "no backing value"
declaration is the auto-incrementing default nobody overrode ([`enums/declaration`](/docs/rules/enums/#declaration "A case with no written value counts on from the one before it, starting at zero")), and a
program that only ever compares cases never has to look at the integer. There is no `string`
backing: a string-valued case would be a heap-allocated, interned buffer where a scalar fits the
value's existing payload for nothing ([`enums/representation`](/docs/rules/enums/#representation "An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is")).

The two backings are told apart everywhere the type is. A `uint`-backed case converts with `as uint`
only, an `int`-backed one with `as int` only, and each refuses the other.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>There is no pure enum and no <code>string</code>-backed enum, and <code>BackedEnum</code> and <code>UnitEnum</code> do not exist</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/enums/#declaration" title="A case with no written value counts on from the one before it, starting at zero"><code>enums/declaration</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#closed-integer-type" title="An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type"><code>enums/closed-integer-type</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#representation" title="An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is"><code>enums/representation</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0010.md">record 0010</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007.md">record 0007</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-syntax/src/parser/tests/decl.rs"><code>crates/nvs-syntax/src/parser/tests/decl.rs</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-codegen/tests/arithmetic.rs"><code>crates/nvs-codegen/tests/arithmetic.rs</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/json-decodes-an-enum-field.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/json-decodes-an-enum-field.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="representation">

## An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#representation"><code>enums/representation</code></a>
</div>

An enum value is its backing integer and nothing more — zero additional bytes over what `int` or
`uint` already costs, no allocation, no refcount, no descriptor. Where the static type is known,
which the type system makes the common case, codegen already knows which enum it is and there is
nothing further to carry.

A runtime tag of its own is **reserved for an enum but not spent**. Materialized into a tagged
value, a case takes the tag of the type backing it, `Int` or `Uint`. A tag only has to answer "which
type is this?" where the static type does not — the `mixed` case, whose representation is still
open. The consequence to obey today: a value that reaches `mixed` is not distinguishable there from
its backing integer, nor one enum from another enum with the same backing.

Crossing an isolate boundary copies a plain scalar, with no object identity to preserve or discard.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>A case is a scalar, so it copies across an isolate boundary like an <code>int</code> and has no identity to preserve</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/enums/#no-class-machinery" title="A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases"><code>enums/no-class-machinery</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#one-backing-type" title="Every enum is backed by exactly one integer type, and nothing else backs one"><code>enums/one-backing-type</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#closed-integer-type" title="An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type"><code>enums/closed-integer-type</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0010.md">record 0010</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007.md">record 0007</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0006.md">record 0006</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0004.md">record 0004</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/json-decodes-an-enum-field.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/json-decodes-an-enum-field.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-fills-an-array-and-survives-a-sort.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-fills-an-array-and-survives-a-sort.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-flows-through-a-generator.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-flows-through-a-generator.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

<div class="nv-rule" id="truthiness">

## An enum case is always truthy, whatever integer backs it

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#truthiness"><code>enums/truthiness</code></a>
</div>

An enum case in a condition is **always truthy**, whatever integer backs it. `Signal::Idle` backed
by `0` is truthy; so is a case backed by a negative value.

An enum follows the object row of the truthy table rather than the integer row its backing type
might suggest ([`enums/representation`](/docs/rules/enums/#representation "An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is")). PHP's enum cases are objects, PHP has no mechanism for
making an object falsy, and so every ported `if ($status)` over an enum has only ever meant "always
true" — judging a case by its backing integer instead would silently change the branch that
condition takes.

Lowering reads this statically: a condition whose static type is an enum needs no truthiness helper
and no comparison at all.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/enums/#representation" title="An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is"><code>enums/representation</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#no-class-machinery" title="A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases"><code>enums/no-class-machinery</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#closed-integer-type" title="An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type"><code>enums/closed-integer-type</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0035.md">record 0035</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0010.md">record 0010</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-codegen/tests/arithmetic.rs"><code>crates/nvs-codegen/tests/arithmetic.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="no-class-machinery">

## A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#no-class-machinery"><code>enums/no-class-machinery</code></a>
</div>

`EnumName::CaseName` **is** an integer constant, inlined at every use site the way a literal `5` is:
nothing is allocated, nothing is refcounted, there is no descriptor, and there is no per-isolate
storage slot for an enum at all ([`enums/representation`](/docs/rules/enums/#representation "An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is")).

An enum body therefore declares only cases and an optional backing type. An `implements` clause is
refused with **`E0218`**; a method, a property, a class constant or a trait use inside the body is
refused with **`E0220`**, which names the class such a member belongs on instead. A case has no
members of its own, and is not an array key — index with `$case as int`.

What stands in for each PHP spelling:

| PHP | Novis |
|---|---|
| `E::A->value` | `E::A as int` (or `as uint`) |
| `E::from($n)` / `E::tryFrom($n)` | `$n as E` / `$n as ?E` |
| `E::A->name` | a `match` of your own |
| `E::cases()` | a `static` method of your own returning `array<E>` |
| methods, constants, `implements` | a class that takes the enum |
| `BackedEnum`, `UnitEnum` | nothing — every enum is integer-backed |

Behaviour over an enum lives on some other class as a `static` method taking the enum, because there
is no standalone-function destination for it to go to.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>No methods, no interfaces, no enum constants, and no <code>::cases()</code>, <code>::from()</code>, <code>::tryFrom()</code>, <code>-&gt;value</code> or <code>-&gt;name</code></p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/enums/#closed-integer-type" title="An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type"><code>enums/closed-integer-type</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#representation" title="An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is"><code>enums/representation</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#no-case-keyword" title="PHP's case keyword does not parse, and each one is diagnosed where it is written"><code>enums/no-case-keyword</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#reflection" title="Reflection describes an enum's shape and grants it nothing a class has"><code>enums/reflection</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0010.md">record 0010</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0008.md">record 0008</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0011.md">record 0011</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-syntax/src/parser/tests/decl.rs"><code>crates/nvs-syntax/src/parser/tests/decl.rs</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-ir/tests/class_constants.rs"><code>crates/nvs-ir/tests/class_constants.rs</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-orders-and-sums-through-its-integer.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/enum/an-enum-orders-and-sums-through-its-integer.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/reject/an-enum-case-is-not-an-array-key.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/reject/an-enum-case-is-not-an-array-key.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="reflection">

## Reflection describes an enum's shape and grants it nothing a class has

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#reflection"><code>enums/reflection</code></a>
</div>

`Core\Reflect\EnumInfo::of(Status::class)` reports an enum's shape as ordinary structural metadata —
the type's name and its closed case list — the same way `ClassInfo` reports a class's shape.

It grants an enum nothing it does not already have: no method dispatch, no interface, no case
identity, and nothing that acts on a value. It is a second description of the same closed integer
type ([`enums/closed-integer-type`](/docs/rules/enums/#closed-integer-type "An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type")), not a reopening of [`enums/no-class-machinery`](/docs/rules/enums/#no-class-machinery "A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases") — a
description of a case list is not a `::cases()` the language does not have.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>There are no case instances for a description to hand back — it carries the type's name and its case list, and nothing that acts</p>
</aside>
